title: Minimum Path Sum
statement:
You are given a grid with `r` rows and `c` columns of non-negative integer costs. You start in the top-left cell and want to reach the bottom-right cell. From any cell you may move only **one step right** or **one step down**.

The cost of a path is the sum of the values of **all** cells on it, including the start and the end cell. Print the minimum possible cost of a path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell.

A plain recursion that tries every path takes exponential time. Work up from the recursive idea to memoisation, then to a bottom-up table, and finally to a version that uses only `O(c)` extra memory.

**Follow-up:** the same idea was also asked as a maximisation (collect as many coins as possible on the way) and with an arbitrary target cell `(x, y)` instead of the bottom-right corner. Think about which parts of your solution change.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `r` and `c`.
Each of the next `r` lines contains `c` space-separated integers: the costs of that row.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum path cost.

examples.explanation: Go right from 5 to 2, down to 1, right to 3, down to 1: 5 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 12. Every other path costs at least 13.
With a single row there is only one path, and it visits every cell: 7 + 0 + 2 + 5 = 14.
Going down first and then right visits only zero-cost cells.

hints: To reach a cell you must have come from the cell above or the cell to its left. Let `best[i][j]` be the cheapest cost of reaching `(i, j)`.
`best[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(best[i-1][j], best[i][j-1])`, with the first row and first column having only one possible predecessor.
Row `i` of the table depends only on row `i - 1` and on the cell just computed to its left, so a single array of length `c` that you update in place is enough.
